sentence: This project develops radiotracers for imaging aggregated alpha synuclein and tau and studies their role in neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson’s disease.
This project studies how the major surface protein of HIV guides itself in infected cells to sites of virus formation and cell-to-cell virus transfer.
This project uses mouse strains with diverse genes to find the genetic features that shape how hosts respond to Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.
This project builds a virtual CT workflow and test datasets of low-dose CT scans to evaluate AI-based imaging products.
This project tries to find out whether substances made by the gut microbiome can prevent muscle atrophy during limb immobilization and help muscle recovery.
This project studies the immune response to syphilis infection and the transcriptome of Treponema pallidum, the bacterium that causes syphilis.
This project provides microscopy support for imaging experiments, including light microscopy and electron microscopy, to cancer researchers.
This project uses imaging to study the structures of respiratory syncytial virus and human metapneumovirus and how they assemble and spread between cells.
This project studies whether stressful experiences with other people are linked to alcohol use motivation, hazardous drinking and anxiety among Hispanic adults.
This project tries to improve distraction osteogenesis, a surgical procedure for bone problems, using a tissue engineering approach.
This project tests bacteria with mutations in different genes to find which genes affect how well bacteria colonize tumors.
This project studies the genetic drivers of Inflammatory Bowel Disease and how they work in the human intestine.
This project builds a platform that measures thousands of chemicals in blood and maps where they collect in human tissues.
This project provides biostatistics and bioinformatics support, such as study design and data analysis, for cancer research.
This project supports clinical trials with children living in rural communities to study disease processes and the effects of medical treatment.
This project uses the roundworm to find out whether the neurons that direct axons to target cells are the same ones that form synapses.
This project tests treatment combinations that target an enzyme that makes the chemotherapy drug Gemcitabine ineffective in high-risk bladder cancer.
This project studies how people receive HIV care and what the outcomes of that care are.
This project tries to protect insulin-producing cells in diabetes by blocking a stress pathway that drives harmful cell failure.
This project studies what blocks retinal ganglion cells and the optic nerve from regrowing after injury.
